scope: Static source review of candidate Android device/common sources after patches 0001-0003; not a final ramdisk audit or proof of no internal writes.

findings.observed: BUILD_WITH_DRMSERVICE :=true includes drmservice, whose init service has class main without disabled; the policy allows read/write on rknand_device and storage_device. Device labels include /dev/rknand_sys_storage and /dev/vendor_storage.
findings.interpretation: Removing rk_store_keybox and drmboot does not remove every automatic process permitted to access non-fstab vendor storage. Source/binary behavior of drmservice is still unreviewed; actual writes were not demonstrated.
findings.recommended_next_change: For an SD test candidate, remove this automatic service and package selection, then inspect the final product inventory and init graph for copies/reintroduction. Do not claim the APK/media DRM services as a whole are disabled merely by removing this separate vendor service.

findings.observed: The default non-Sofia common config selects Broadcom/ap6xxx and Bluetooth; init.connectivity is copied under that selection, then chmod/chown grants Bluetooth ownership of /dev/vflash and /dev/vendor_storage. ueventd also grants Bluetooth /dev/vflash and Bluetooth policy allows rw. TV product directly lists Bluetooth.
findings.interpretation: The selection is a source default, not identification of the actual Wi-Fi chip. Removing only init chmod lines is incomplete because ueventd/policy and packages independently retain access.
findings.recommended_next_change: The final Vortex product requires no Bluetooth: remove BT package/feature, init grants and services, ueventd grant and matching policy in an explicit profile. Keep the unknown actual Wi-Fi identity separate; do not select a new Wi-Fi driver based on these defaults.

findings.observed: whtest.sh is copied unconditionally to /system/bin; its active command remounts /dev/block/mtdblock8 over /system RW and removes system/app/*.nm.
findings.interpretation: No automatic init service invoking whtest was found in the examined source trees. This is an executable dangerous path remaining in the product, not a demonstrated boot-time write.
findings.recommended_next_change: Omit this factory test script from the first SD product and inspect final /system/bin rather than relying only on init triggers.

findings.observed: preinstall_cleanup.sh is copied unconditionally; it remounts /system RW, deletes /system/preinstall_del entries and remounts RO.
findings.interpretation: This follows the mounted /system rather than an explicit internal block device, so a correct SD mount points it at the SD. It still violates a simple assumption that ro fstab implies no subsequent system mutation. No automatic caller was found in the trees reviewed; the corresponding framework/package implementation is outside this checkout.
findings.recommended_next_change: Omit this factory cleanup script for first SD media or establish and audit all callers before inclusion.

findings.observed: Recovery defaults to TARGET_NO_RECOVERY ?= false and Rockchip recovery true. Its init imports mode-specific files and automatically starts recovery. Common recovery.sd.fstab actually uses ff0f0000.rksdmmc for critical and boot/loader partitions; the device recovery.sd.fstab uses ff500000.rksdmmc instead. Existing recovery mode files mount internal legacy paths and load NAND/drmboot modules. mkimage.sh packages recovery when a recovery/root exists.
findings.interpretation: The name recovery.sd.fstab alone proves no safe SD target. The final build rules choosing the fstab are absent; no selection was established. Setting TARGET_NO_RECOVERY in a product may not by itself remove inherited source/prebuilt artifacts or flashing routes.
findings.recommended_next_change: Exclude recovery from the first media and exclude recovery/OTA payloads from its packager; audit the resolved build target and final ramdisk/images. Do not copy or repair the common recovery fstab by guessing physical storage.

findings.observed: The normal init has a literal import of init.optee.rc; that file defines a class core tee-supplicant and its policy permits rw of uboot and rpmb block devices with sys_rawio. Fixed labels identify mmcblk1 and mmcblk1rpmb by enumeration. The device BoardConfig sets PRODUCT_HAVE_OPTEE := false. No PRODUCT_COPY_FILES copying init.optee.rc was found in these examined device/common makefiles.
findings.interpretation: The service is not proven present in the final ramdisk; it must not be described as an active confirmed writer. Its import is a residual expansion point, and an inherited OP-TEE package could supply it independently.
findings.recommended_next_change: Explicitly exclude OP-TEE init/binaries for the first media when not required and verify the final ramdisk; never use mmc numbering as a board identity proof.

findings.observed: The normal board init imports init.${ro.hardware}.bootmode.${ro.bootmode}.rc and SD init calls mount_all fstab.rk30board; the product packages only fstab.rk30board.bootmode.sd after patch.
findings.interpretation: Correct ro.bootmode and creation/selection of /fstab.rk30board depend on platform system/core and boot arguments. Removing fallback files does not prove a failed mount halts boot or prevent other services from starting.
findings.recommended_next_change: Resolve platform init implementation, reject mismatched/missing media claims for SD profile, and inspect actual mount sources before enabling any write-capable service or diagnostic collector.

findings.observed: The vendor copy list includes librockchip_update_jni.so. No complete updater APK/service or caller graph was available in these source checkouts.
findings.interpretation: A copied library is not itself a running updater; the final product may include callers from unresolved platform/device/vendor projects.
findings.recommended_next_change: Audit the complete resolved package/library/service inventory, exclude update/install/flash routes from the first external-test product, and inspect the generated media manifest.

logging_design.status: Design only; not implemented or runtime validated.
existing_observations: common/init.rk30board.rc:43 creates /data/logs as 0755 root:shell in post-fs-data.
common/init.rk30board.rc:227-235 defines vendor abc collector, disabled by default and toggled through persist.sys.abc_switch; source unavailable and overly broad permissions for this purpose.
common/sepolicy/abc.te grants sys_module/sys_admin, kernel syslog_mod and executable tool access; do not reuse the domain as a least-privilege Vortex collector.
common/sepolicy/apk_logfs.te:3-16 provides debug-only logging policy, but the service seen in init.sofiaboard.rc is a different hardware target, not proof it runs for rk30board.
recommended_flow: Build an explicit userdebug-only Vortex collector domain and executable/script with fixed output paths and bounded rotation. Do not enable permissive SELinux or copy the broad abc/crashlogd policy.

Start only after post-fs-data and an affirmative verified SD mount identity for /data and /system. Use /proc/self/mountinfo and major/minor + sysfs/controller resolution rather than /dev/mmcblk enumeration alone. Check the expected read-only /system flag; fail closed for absent/ambiguous inputs.

Place a bounded boot snapshot (cmdline, mountinfo, dmesg, getprop limited to boot/hardware/build, exact source commit) and rotated logcat on /data/logs/vortex or another dedicated label. Data stays on SD only if mount identity was independently confirmed.

For failures before SD /data is mounted, keep diagnostics in RAM or use a separately prepared and verified log partition; do not fall back to internal /cache or /data. Existing recovery is not a collector.

Wait for system log service readiness or retry within bounded limits. Use standard Android logcat rotation and a fixed directory, sanitize filenames, prevent symlink-following, control ownership/mode, and avoid collecting all credentials/properties unnecessarily.
The operator should only need to start the resulting prepared media; no new manual FlashID, Wi-Fi, board photos or dumps are requested.
selinux_requirements: Define executable + dedicated data type and init_daemon_domain; grant only logd socket access, necessary proc/sysfs/kernel log reads and writes under the dedicated output label.
No block_device:blk_file write, no rknand/storage/vflash access, no sys_rawio, no sys_module, no sys_admin, no broad domain/device permissive exemptions.
Compile the policy with the actual Android platform revision and run enforcing tests on the generated system before declaring automatic SD logging functional.
dmesg/kernel log access is privileged; granting read does not imply syslog_mod. If the platform only offers a combined wrapper, keep behavior read-only and verify.
limits: A collector starting after data mount cannot diagnose every boot failure; a claimed always-available log capture would be false.
A correct fstab is only a static input and not sufficient proof that /data is mounted on the physical SD.
Raw access by kernel/vendor processes must be considered even if the logger itself writes only SD.

first_media_acceptance_gates: Resolve a complete platform, generated product and init import graph.
Reject inconsistent boot media inputs; ensure mount sources match externally selected controller/partition mapping.
Exclude recovery, factory tools, automatic vendor provisioning, update/flash routes and Bluetooth from the explicit first test product.
Inspect actual boot ramdisk, system file list, service triggers, SELinux policy, kernel config and media layout; source patches alone do not pass this gate.
Only after an image exists and passes these checks supply exact SD preparation instructions; do not present a generic reference kernel/DTB as image.
Run physical boot tests later without writing internal memory; no hardware activity occurred in this review.
